intro: The 1990s began with democratic openings and ended in the Rwandan genocide and the Congo wars. Africa then built new continental institutions, faced the Arab Spring in 2011 and produced its newest state, South Sudan, which fell into civil war. This module covers events to October 2026, and the latest are unsettled.
outcomes: Explain how the categories Hutu and Tutsi hardened under colonial rule and after independence, without the Hamitic myth.
Narrate the genocide of 1994, the international failure, and handle the death toll as a range that depends on its baseline.
Explain how the AU's Article 4(h) differs from the OAU's non-interference and name one limit.
Assess whether the Arab Spring 'failed' in Africa, with criteria.
Mark recent events [check current] and avoid presenting them as settled.

lessons.title: Rwanda before 1994: how the categories hardened

blocks.x: Content notice: this lesson and the next deal with genocide. The sources are used for understanding.
From social labels to racial categories

'Tutsi' first described a person rich in cattle and 'Hutu' a follower of a more powerful person. {{hrw-rwanda}} Pre-Colonial Africa, Module 6, traces how the hierarchy grew between the seventeenth and nineteenth centuries.
German ethnographers gave the Tutsi a supposed Hamitic origin from outside Africa. That was a colonial racial theory, now discredited, and not a fact. {{rd-interwar}}

In the 1920s the Belgians gave office to Tutsi alone and shut Hutu out of higher education, acting on racial theories such as the 'Hamitic hypothesis' rather than on a plan to divide and rule. {{hrw-rwanda}} Hutu had almost no route to higher education except the Catholic seminaries until 1956. {{rd-elite}}
In the 1930s everyone was registered by group, and about 15 per cent declared themselves Tutsi, 84 per cent Hutu and 1 per cent Twa. {{hrw-rwanda}}

The date of the identity cards differs between sources: one survey gives 1926, {{rd-interwar}} while most Rwanda historians date compulsory ethnic cards to the mid-1930s (our check). The popular 'ten cows' rule for registration is not correct, though 1930s tax rules did distinguish owners of ten or more cattle. {{hrw-rwanda}} Say only that Belgium made ethnic identity a legal category in the 1930s.

Colonial codification of chiefs and 'tribal' units created fixed ethnic identities on one reading; specialists agree that colonial rule hardened identities but argue that the categories existed in some form before it [CONTESTED]. {{rd-interwar}}
The revolution of 1959 to 1962

The Hutu Manifesto of 03/1957 denounced the political monopoly of the Tutsi. {{rd-elite}} The Belgians turned from the Tutsi in the 1950s, and violence in 11/1959 killed several hundred. {{hrw-rwanda}}
Another count gives 200 to 270 killed in 11/1959, over 1,200 arrests and about 7,000 people made victims of destruction. {{gha-viii-ch08}}

In the communal elections of 07/1960 the Parmehutu party won 210 of 229 communes, the republic was declared at Gitarama on 28/01/1961, and independence came on 01/07/1962 with Kayibanda as president. {{rd-indep}} In 09/1961 about 80 per cent voted to end the monarchy. {{hrw-rwanda}}
About 20,000 Tutsi were killed and over 300,000 fled by 1967. {{hrw-rwanda}} Ethnic quotas of 9 per cent applied in schools and jobs. {{rd-indep}}
The run-up, 1973 to 1993
Habyarimana took power in a coup on 05/07/1973. {{rd-indep}} Coffee gave 75 per cent of Rwanda's foreign exchange and its price fell at the end of the 1980s. {{hrw-rwanda}}
The Rwandan Patriotic Front, formed by exiles in Uganda, invaded in 1990. {{lib}} The attack on Kigali on the night of 04/10/1990 was staged, and about 13,000 people were arrested. {{hrw-rwanda}}
Killings in Kibilira, the north-west and Bugesera from 1990 to 1993 left about 2,000 Tutsi dead, and no one was convicted. {{hrw-rwanda}}
Propaganda prepared in public
The newspaper Kangura attacked the RPF and Tutsi from 10/1990. The radio station RTLM began broadcasting in 08/1993. About 29 per cent of households had a radio in 1991. {{hrw-rwanda}}

Two techniques recur: 'created' events, such as the staged attack on Kigali, and 'accusation in a mirror', blaming the enemy for what one plans. Léon Mugesera's speech of 22/11/1992 called on a party meeting to 'exterminate this scum'. {{hrw-rwanda}}
An army memorandum of 21/09/1992 defined 'the enemy' as the Tutsi. In 07/1991 donors had declined to make removing ethnic classification from identity cards a condition of aid. {{hrw-rwanda}}

The Arusha Accords of 08/1993 gave the RPF 40 per cent of the troops and 50 per cent of the high command. {{rd-indep}} Habyarimana had called the talks' agreements 'a scrap of paper' on 15/11/1992. {{hrw-rwanda}}

blocks.q: A documentary says the genocide came from 'ancient tribal hatred'. Which evidence answers that best?
o: The categories were social labels hardened into legal race by colonial rule, and the killing was prepared through propaganda and organisation from 1990
blocks.w: Hardened categories and prepared propaganda, not age-old hatred. {{hrw-rwanda}}

blocks.q: A source says the 'ten cows' rule decided who was registered as Tutsi. What should you say?
o: It is not correct for registration, though 1930s tax rules did distinguish owners of ten or more cattle
blocks.w: Check a popular story against specialist research. {{hrw-rwanda}}

i: Hutu and Tutsi were social labels made into legal categories in the 1930s. {{hrw-rwanda}}
The Hamitic origin story was a colonial racial theory. {{rd-interwar}}
The killing was prepared in public from 1990, through propaganda and massacres.

lessons.title: The genocide of 1994 and its toll

blocks.title: Events from 1994 to the present
blocks.cap: Approximate spans; open ends are not settled [check current].

blocks.x: One hundred days

The plane carrying President Habyarimana was shot down on 06/04/1994, and killing began the next day. {{lib}} Who shot down the plane is [CONTESTED], since French and Rwandan inquiries reached different conclusions. {{lib}}

Orders passed from the prime minister to prefects and burgomasters, who read them out at local meetings, and umuganda communal labour was turned to killing. Machetes were imported in numbers enough to arm every third adult Hutu male. {{hrw-rwanda}}

In the centre and south many Hutu at first refused to kill and had to be coerced. The genocide was a campaign in which participants were recruited over time, not a spontaneous outburst. {{hrw-rwanda}}
The RPF took Kigali on 04/07/1994, over a million refugees crossed into Zaire by 17/07/1994, and the Government of National Unity was sworn in on 19/07/1994. {{carlsson}}
The international failure
A cable of 11/01/1994 warned of plans to exterminate Tutsi, and its handling was criticised by the UN's own inquiry. {{carlsson}}
The UN force was one third the size first recommended, and the US and the UK in 02/1994 refused a stronger mandate that would add cost. {{hrw-rwanda}}

Ten Belgian peacekeepers were killed on 07/04/1994, Belgium withdrew its troops, and on 21/04/1994 the Security Council voted unanimously to cut the UN force under General Romeo Dallaire from 2,539 to 270 while the killing was known. {{carlsson}}

Dallaire and other military experts said 5,000 experienced soldiers could have ended the genocide even in the later weeks. Officials avoided the word genocide and spoke of 'chaos' and 'tribal' killing. {{hrw-rwanda}}

Operation Turquoise was authorised on 22/06/1994 by 10 votes with 5 abstentions and was not under UN command. {{carlsson}} About 2,500 French troops saved 15,000 to 17,000 lives, but also let genocidal officials flee. {{hrw-rwanda}}

The UN inquiry found the overriding failure was a lack of resources and political will, and called for an apology. {{carlsson}} In 2021 a French commission found heavy and overwhelming responsibilities in France's policy, without finding complicity in the genocide itself. {{lib}}

blocks.title: Worked example: the baseline decides the toll (our arithmetic)
steps: HRW: 657,000 before, about 150,000 survivors, so about 507,000 dead, which is 507,000 over 657,000, about 77 per cent.
Reader: 930,000 before, about 130,000 survivors, so about 800,000 dead, which is 86 per cent.
The two baselines differ by 273,000 (930,000 minus 657,000), and that difference drives most of the gap between the tolls.
Write: at least half a million and perhaps 800,000 or more, depending on the pre-genocide Tutsi population [ESTIMATE, CONTESTED].

blocks.x: Tolls at single sites vary by a factor of ten or more: at Bisesero as many as 50,000 were said to have died, against a list of just over 5,100 names. {{hrw-rwanda}}

The RPF also committed grave violations in 1994. A UNHCR investigator estimated 25,000 to 45,000 killed by the RPF between 04/1994 and 08/1994, and the UN agreed to suppress his report in 09/1994. HRW says it has too little data to confirm the figure, and contrasts the genocidal campaign, which ran through the whole machinery of the state, with the RPF's military campaign. Both sets of crimes are recorded. {{hrw-rwanda}}

lessons.title: Justice, the Congo wars and the African Union

blocks.x: Justice
The International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda, from 1994 in Arusha, tried senior leaders. Rwanda's gacaca community courts (2002 to 2012) handled well over a million cases. {{lib}}

UN and human rights bodies have documented RPF killings after 1994, such as at Kibeho in 1995. The present government's limits on political space are widely criticised, and the government rejects the criticism [CONTESTED]. {{lib}}
The Congo wars
After the genocide, Hutu perpetrators and civilians fled into eastern Zaire. In 1996 to 1997 Rwanda, Uganda and others backed Laurent Kabila's rebellion, which ended Mobutu's rule. {{lib}}
The Second Congo War (1998 to 2003) drew in about nine states and many armed groups. Deaths from violence, hunger and disease are given at several million [ESTIMATE, CONTESTED]. {{lib}}
The widely cited International Rescue Committee figure of about 5.4 million excess deaths has been criticised for method. Fighting in the east continues [check current]. {{lib}}

An early popular history gives only 'a million or more' for the Congo wars and explains Africa's troubles partly by hero worship of strongmen and a long history of indigenous slavery. These are one author's interpretations, not a consensus. {{hs-after}}
From OAU to AU
The Constitutive Act (2000) came into force in 2001, and the AU was launched in Durban on 09/07/2002. Muammar Gaddafi pressed for rapid union and Thabo Mbeki shaped the institutions. {{lib}}

blocks.title: Worked example: from principle to practice
steps: Article 4(h) lets the Union intervene in grave circumstances; the OAU barred interference.
Ask how often the clause has been used, who pays, and which states vote for it.
The usual tool in practice is suspension of states after coups, and money and member-state reluctance restrict action.
Say: the principle changed more than the practice did [CONTESTED].

blocks.q: In 2003 a member state begins killing a minority. Under the OAU's rules and under the AU's Article 4(h), what could each organisation do?
o: The OAU barred interference; the AU may intervene in grave cases such as genocide, though money and reluctance limit it
blocks.w: That is the break from non-interference. {{lib}}

blocks.title: Worked example: a verdict with criteria (illustrative)
steps: Statement: the Arab Spring failed in Africa.
Criteria: regime change, democratic outcome, stability, rights.
Tunisia: change and a democratic opening, then rollback. Egypt: change, then new authoritarianism. Libya: change, then conflict and fragmentation.
Verdict: mixed. It succeeded on removing rulers, failed on stable democracy in most cases, and later movements show that the process continued [CONTESTED].

lessons.title: Sudan, South Sudan and the unsettled present

blocks.x: Everything in this lesson is [check current]. Source note: these sentences reflect sources read on the dates given and not reopened since. Treat them as a snapshot.
South Sudan

Sudan's wars between north and south (1955 to 1972 and 1983 to 2005) ended with the Comprehensive Peace Agreement of 09/01/2005. A January 2011 referendum gave about 98.8 per cent for independence, and South Sudan became independent on 09/07/2011. {{lib}}
Pre-Colonial Africa, Module 2, shows that the north-south line had long been a shifting zone of identity rather than a fixed racial frontier.

Civil war began in December 2013 between President Salva Kiir and Riek Machar. Deaths are estimated in the hundreds of thousands, with one study putting it at about 400,000 by 2018 [ESTIMATE]. {{lib}}
In September 2026 Kiir dissolved the transitional government; Machar is detained and on trial, and elections are scheduled for 22/12/2026 [check current]. {{lib}}
Sudan

Since April 2023 the Sudanese army and the Rapid Support Forces have fought a war that aid workers say has killed over 200,000 people and displaced millions. Drone strikes are now a main cause of civilian deaths, and El Fasher fell to the RSF in October 2025 [check current]. {{lib}}

A UN news item of 21/10/2026 says the war between the army and the RSF, former allies in a 2021 coup, is in its fourth year, that almost 34 million people need humanitarian support and eight million children are out of school, and that the sixth round of consultative talks in Geneva had neither belligerent present. It gives no death toll [check current]. {{dppa-sudan}}
The Sahel
Military takeovers since 2020 in Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger, and in Guinea and Gabon, have challenged AU norms and regional bodies [check current]. {{lib}}
